exam.title: Developing in Agentic AI Systems
exam.audience: Practitioners operating, integrating, supervising, and governing AI agents inside production-grade SDLC workflows using GitHub as control plane.
exam.passScore: Microsoft certification exams generally require 700 or greater; confirm on the official exam page before sitting.

domains.title: Prepare agent architecture and SDLC processes
domains.whatExamTests: Whether you can design safe agentic SDLC workflows before the agent acts, using GitHub as the control plane for scope, evidence, review, and delivery speed.

groups.title: Integrate agents into the software development lifecycle (SDLC)
skills: Identify steps for agents to perform
Identify and mitigate common anti-patterns in agents
Define inputs, outputs, and success criteria for agents

groups.title: Define boundaries between planning, reasoning, and action
skills: Configure agent planning to be distinct from agent execution
Configure an agent to output a structured plan
Validate agent plans
Prevent agent action until the agent checked and approved

groups.title: Configure observability and control for autonomous agents
skills: Plan and implement the degree of agent autonomy, including guardrails
Configure agent to produce inspectable artifacts within standard development tooling
Configure human intervention for autonomous agents without slowing delivery

domains.title: Implement tool use and environment interaction
domains.whatExamTests: Whether you can connect agents to tools and environments without over-permissioning them, and can design safe execution paths with traceable failure handling.

groups.title: Select and configure agent tools
skills: Identify required tools
Configure agent tools
Configure agent tool permissions

groups.title: Configure MCP servers
skills: Add an MCP server as a tool to an agent
Configure a GitHub remote MCP server
Configure the MCP registries
Configure MCP allow lists

groups.title: Integrate agents within development environments
skills: Evaluate the execution context for an agent
Configure an agent's scope to a specific repository
Configure an agent to be invoked in a CI workflow
Configure an agent to use branch-based scope
Enable an agent to perform autonomous actions, including creating branches and pull requests
Configure an agent to handle environment-specific constraints

groups.title: Operate agents with safe execution paths and robust error handling
skills: Implement error handling
Implement retries
Implement rollbacks
Implement escalation paths
Implement traceability and accountability for agent actions

domains.title: Manage memory, state, and execution
domains.whatExamTests: Whether you can keep agent context useful, current, auditable, scoped, and portable across interruptions, tools, and multi-agent work.

groups.title: Implement agent memory strategies
skills: Choose between short-term, long-term, and external memory
Scope agent memory to task-relevant information
Define memory expiration, pruning, and reset rules

groups.title: Persist agent state and manage context drift
skills: Capture task progress and decisions as durable artifacts
Resume agent work without repeating steps or diverging from prior decisions
Detect and correct drift during extended agent execution

groups.title: Ensure continuity of agent memory and state across tools and environments
skills: Share agent state
Prevent conflicting context
Prevent stale context

domains.title: Perform evaluation, error analysis, and tuning
domains.whatExamTests: Whether you can evaluate agent work through evidence, classify failure causes, and tune instructions, memory, tools, and workflows without hiding defects.

groups.title: Define success criteria and evaluation signals for agent tasks
skills: Specify expected outcomes and operational constraints for agent tasks
Identify qualitative and quantitative evaluation signals to evaluate agents
Align evaluation criteria with development intent
Generate evaluation signals by using automated scanning tools

groups.title: Analyze agent failures and identify root causes
skills: Identify failures by using logs, plans, traces, outputs, and workflow artifacts
Classify root causes, including reasoning errors, tool misuse, and context or environment issues

groups.title: Tune agent behavior based on evaluation results
skills: Revise instructions, workflows, or constraints
Refine memory usage
Refine tool usage and tool access

domains.title: Orchestrate multi-agent coordination
domains.whatExamTests: Whether you can coordinate multiple agents safely, isolate parallel work, capture handoffs, detect conflicts, and manage agent lifecycle changes without losing auditability.

groups.title: Operate and manage multi-agent workflows
skills: Apply an orchestration pattern to coordinate multiple agents
Configure agent isolation for parallel execution
Detect and resolve agent conflicts, including overlapping code changes, duplicated effort, and contradictory outputs

groups.title: Configure observability for multi-agent behavior by using logs, artifacts, and operational signals
skills: Configure multi-agent workflows to produce artifacts suitable for review and audit
Document key decisions, handoffs, and outcomes across agents
Perform post-hoc analysis of multi-agent behavior

groups.title: Detect and respond to multi-agent failures and degraded behavior
skills: Identify failed, partial, or stalled agent executions
Respond to degraded behavior or coordination across agents
Implement multi-agent recovery patterns, including rollback and human-in-the-loop

groups.title: Manage the lifecycle of agents within multi-agent workflows
skills: Add agents to existing multi-agent workflows
Update, reconfigure, or replace agents without disrupting active workflows
Retire agents while preserving auditability and workflow continuity

domains.title: Implement guardrails and accountability
domains.whatExamTests: Whether you can right-size autonomy, enforce least privilege, block unsafe actions, keep humans accountable, and preserve evidence without creating approval theatre.

groups.title: Define autonomy levels
skills: Classify agent actions by operational, security, and compliance risk to right-size human interventions
Assign autonomy levels to maximize delivery speed while remaining compliant with organizational security and Responsible AI standards

groups.title: Implement guardrails and human-in-the-loop workflows
skills: Identify the subset of actions that require human judgment
Block actions that violate defined security, compliance, or Responsible AI policies
Scope permissions and execution contexts to enforce least-privilege access
Require explicit authorization or controlled paths for irreversible or compliance-sensitive changes
Preserve execution velocity by minimizing approvals that do not materially reduce risk
